newsitem.title: PERU: Peru coffee exporter says output short of demand.
newsitem.headline: Peru coffee exporter says output short of demand.

text.p: Production of Peruvian "green" coffee will fall well short of demand this year due mainly to climatic factors, a leading exporter said Wednesday.

Alberto Arribas, manager of local firm Peru Cafe, said the country's total exports of "green" coffee, the main local export variety, would likely reach 1.5 million quintales (69,000 tonnes) in 1996, 32 percent less than last year.
He attributed this to the affects of a drought at the end of 1995, throughout the country but especially in the north, which harmed this year's harvests.
Arribas added that in the first seven months of this year, Peru exported 1.44 million quintales (66,378 tonnes) of "green" coffee.

"According to the estimates, there are only another 57,000 quintales (2,622 tonnes) of green coffee left to export between September and December," said Arribas. "In order to comply with international commitments, exporters of Peruvian green coffee now have to pay (to producers) $10 or $15 more per quintal."
Last year, Peru exported a record 2.22 million quintales (102,074 tonnes), up from 1.45 million quintales (66,654 tonnes) in 1994.
